comment: How the player is built, once, for every target. scripts/build_player.py builds it; scripts/prepare_rmlui.py builds the same RmlUi (and FreeType) for the tests. A difference between targets is a key under a target here, never a second script.

configure.comment-windows-x86_64: No WinMM: it is only RetroArch's MIDI output, which the macOS player does not have (its build never enables CoreMIDI, so its MIDI driver is null), and it opens the system's synthesiser at every start, which slows the launch.

makefile.comment-windows-x86_64: Os: the player's own code is optimised for size, which makes it smaller without slowing emulation, because the core does the work. RmlUi stays Release: built MinSizeRel it requires a std::string constructor the static C++ runtime does not have. -ffunction-sections with --gc-sections makes the player larger with this toolchain.

drivers.comment: What an exported game's player is told to use, per platform: its audio driver, its controller driver, and the controller profile folders RetroArch reads. A pad's profiles are read from the folder named for the driver it was connected under; on Windows that driver connects XInput pads as xinput and every other pad as dinput. The exporter writes audio and joypad into the game's settings; scripts/build_kit.py stages joypadProfiles from the pinned autoconfig archive (scripts/prepare_runtime.py).

systemLibraries.comment: The libraries every machine of a platform has, so a player, a launcher or a core may import them. The Windows list covers every import of the catalog's Windows cores, as published on the buildbot, and of the builder. scripts/build_player.py rejects a player, launcher or preview renderer that imports anything else, scripts/build_builder.py a builder or command line, and an export rejects such a core. Names are lower case; Windows also resolves any api-ms-win- API set.

launcher.comment: The game's launcher, for a target that runs it as its own program: its shared sources at the top of desktop/src-tauri/launcher and its platform's entry in the folder named for the platform. A macOS launcher is built into the app at export when its kit does not contain one.

fileLayer.comment: libretro's file layer, which the menu reads and writes its files through with UTF-8 paths on every platform, named from the fork's root. Every program built from the menu's sources links it. The config reader, file/config_file.c, is not part of it, so a test program can stand in for that boundary.

preview.comment: The builder's menu preview, rml-preview: the player's own RmlUi renderer drawing a composed menu into a picture, in an OpenGL context on a window never shown, built beside the player from the same fork, RmlUi and FreeType, and with the file layer above. 'sources' are the repository's, 'forkSources' the fork's; a target adds its OpenGL context. The menu GL probe (test_dcmenu.py) draws in the same context. 'install' says how it reaches the builder's resources: copy, for a program linked with everything it needs; freeze, for one that carries its libraries in a Frameworks folder beside it (rominabox-cli freeze-macos-executable, as the macOS kit's player).

kit.comment: What scripts/build_kit.py puts in a target's runtime kit besides the assets every kit carries (scripts/kit_assets.py). A file is named by its role, which the exporter reads it by, and says where in the kit it goes. A source is build: a file in the player build, or toolchain: a file in the toolchain's installation. A target whose player links libraries the system lacks names 'libraries': the kit folder they are copied into, beside the player, and where they are installed; each goes with the licence files its installation carries.

windows-x86_64.runtime: the MinGW-w64 runtime: its C runtime, winpthreads and the GCC runtime (native/MinGW-w64-runtime.txt, native/winpthreads-COPYING.txt, native/GCC-runtime-exception.txt)
